method.classes: Regex/brace-matching scanner (cxxscan.py) over `git archive 47f13dadb` of avida-core/source and include: comments, strings and preprocessor lines are blanked, scopes tracked by braces; top-level (non-nested) class/struct/union definitions and namespaces containing functions are entries; files with functions but no class become `free_functions` entries. `lines` = class extent in its header/.cc + bodies of out-of-line `Class::method` definitions anywhere (file_lines gives whole-file totals; macro-generated code is invisible except for the action macros). Template specialisations with the same qualified name in one file are merged.
method.depends_on: Heuristic: identifiers inside the class extent and its out-of-line method bodies that equal the name of another known entry (ambiguous short names resolved by namespace); `includes` lists resolved #include targets of the class files. Coarse by design; over-approximates (e.g. forward uses) and misses macro-generated references.
method.build_status: Parsed from avida-core/CMakeLists.txt: `built` = a .cc in AVIDA_CORE_SOURCES / VIEWERCORE_SOURCES / avida target, or (header-only) a header reachable by #include closure from those; `optional_target` = only in targets whose option defaults OFF (avida-viewer, avida-text, unit-tests); `not_in_cmake` = .cc exists but is in no source list; `unreachable` = header never included by compiled code. source/script/* is not_in_cmake (no avida-s target) yet is required by the 28 _asl_ tests.
method.target_crate: mapping.py: directory + explicit name tables following ARCHITECTURE.md layer table. `analyze` is used as a crate (Status table) although the layer table lists analyze mode under `world`.
method.port_status: Rust doc/line comments are searched for the C++ name (unprefixed Avida:: classes need a qualified citation). `strong` = comment with a port marker (Port/C++:/mirror/Replaces/`Name::method`) or in a //! header. Evidence must be in a file of the class's target crate, else not_started (cited from other crates only). Method-name coverage = share of the class's method lines whose snake_case name (or Get/Set/Is-stripped variant) exists as a fn in the citing files or is cited as `Class::method`. In crates ARCHITECTURE.md marks "ported and gated" (apto, config, genome, tasks, environment, phenotype, resources) and in `script`, any class with strong in-crate evidence is `ported`; elsewhere ported needs coverage >= 0.75, else `partial`; file-name-only matches are `partial`. A few big classes in crates marked "in progress" (cPopulation, cStats, cWorld, cDeme, cPopulationCell, cBirthChamber, cOrganism, cHardwareBase, cHardwareCPU) are forced to `partial`. `n/a` = target none/obsolete. Action classes: ported = parsed by actions.rs and (stats actions) printer fn exists; partial = parsed only.
method.actions: Registrations: regex over `action_lib->Register<Class>("Name")` outside // comments (432; 4 more are commented out). STATS_OUT_FILE / POP_OUT_FILE macro-generated classes are recovered from their invocations (class_lines = 1 invocation line; macro definition is shared). Description = literal text of GetDescription. `touches` = regex tags over the class body (and macro body): driver, landscape, test_cpu, demes, systematics, environment(+resources), population(+organisms), stats, output_files, rng_config; `touches_summary` is `stats only` when tags are within {stats, output_files}, else the highest-priority tag (driver > landscape > test_cpu > demes > systematics > environment > population). tests_using = number of test_matrix.json tests listing the action (case-insensitive, as cActionLibrary lower-cases keys). parsed_by_actions_rs = name in STATS_OUT_FILE_ACTIONS or OTHER_ACTIONS of crates/world/src/actions.rs.
method.instructions: Instruction tables are the `s_f_array` initialisers (regex on tInstLibEntry<tMethod>(...) and the INST/INSTI macros of GP8). Handler lines = body length of the method in the class (or cHardwareBase). Each test's instruction sets are resolved from avida.cfg (+ -def/-set args): inline INSTSET/INST blocks, `#include INST_SET=file` mappings, or legacy files via INST_SET + HARDWARE_TYPE (cHardwareManager::ConvertLegacyInstSetFile); hardware type comes from the INSTSET `hw_type=` or HARDWARE_TYPE. tests_using counts tests whose resolved instruction sets list the name. Rust handler detection: normalised `"Inst_X"` string or `fn inst_x` in crates/hardware (excluding cpu_inst_lib.rs, which is only the table).
method.stats_printers: All out-of-line `cStats::Print*` definitions in cStats.cc; ported = a `fn print_<snake>` of the same normalised name in crates/world/src/stats*.rs; tests = tests using the action with the same name as the method (all stats actions are named after the method).
method.tests: Config values from each test's avida.cfg (+ -set/-def/-c args) compared with defaults parsed from cAvidaConfig.h CONFIG_ADD_VAR; features are derived from settings, actions, instruction names, analyze.cfg commands and environment.cfg (see assemble_all.py). Action names in test_matrix.json that are not registered and look like file names/arguments are ignored; identifier-like unregistered names are reported. tests dir read from the 47f13dadb archive, except analyze_printphenotypes_grouping and manager_provider_id_dispatch which only exist in the working tree.
method.blocked_by: Per test: core classes (cWorld, cPopulation, ..., listed in assemble_all.py BASE) + hardware class + every instruction handler of its instruction sets + feature classes (feature -> class table; features without a class get a nominal 300-line item) + every action used (not parsed, or stats printer missing). Items with status != ported block. Cost = remaining lines (not_started: lines; partial: lines * (1 - method coverage), min 10%; handlers: handler lines; action: class lines + printer lines).
method.port_order: Only tests with expected output that load on this commit (no unregistered action names, resolvable instruction set) are scheduled. Step 0 = items blocking every scheduled test. Then greedy: repeatedly add the blocker set of the test that maximises (tests newly fully unblocked) / (remaining cost), ties by count then cost. Costs are C++ line counts, a proxy for effort.
method.unblocked_by_heads_core_actions: Tests of kind `run` whose only hardware is cHardwareCPU, whose features are within {resources, reaction_requisites, test_on_divide}, all of whose actions are registered and parsed by actions.rs, with all of: core population bundle (BASE classes), cHardwareCPU with all its instruction handlers, the heads-bundle test CPU classes. `strict_printer` variant additionally requires every stats-printer action's cStats method to be ported. `no_test_cpu` variant excludes tests needing the test CPU (test-on-divide, PrintDominantGenotype etc.).
